choice.ex: (A) preserved (B) luck (C) drives 근거 ❹❺❼ 해설: (A) ❹ wil tend to be perpetuated = 보존 / (B) ❺ it is a matter of chance = 운 / (C) ❼ Through endless repetition of this cycle … organisms evolve = 진화를 이끎. eliminated는 ❹(영속됨)와 반대, design(의도·설계)은 ❺의 chance와 반대, halts(멈추게 하다)는 ❼ organisms evolve와 반대. 요약문 해석: 세포가 분열할 때, 작은 복제 오류들이 종종 그 유전체에 슬며시 끼어든다. 세포의 전망을 개선하는 오류는 (A) 보존되는 경향이 있고, 돕지도 해치지도 않는 오류는 (B) 운에 따라 살아남거나 사라지며, 심각하게 해로운 오류는 그것을 지닌 세포와 함께 사라진다. 끝없이 반복되는 이러한 변이의 선 별이 진화를 (C) 이끄는 것이다.
choice.psg: ❶ When a cell divides, the genomes of its two daughters are often not quite identical to each other or to that of the parent cell. ❷ On rare occasions, the error may represent a change for the better; more probably, it will cause no significant difference in the cell’s prospects. ❸ But in some cases, the error will cause serious damage; for example, by disrupting the coding sequence for a key protein. ❹ Changes due to mistakes of the first type will tend to be perpetuated, because the altered cell has an increased likelihood of reproducing itself. ❺ Changes due to mistakes of the second type ― neutral changes ― may be perpetuated or not: it is a matter of chance whether the altered cell or its cousins will succeed. ❻ But changes that cause serious damage lead nowhere: the cell that suffers them dies, leaving no progeny. ❼ Through endless repetition of this cycle of mutation and natural selection organisms evolve: their genetic specifications change, sometimes giving organisms new ways to exploit the environment more effectively, to survive in competition with others, and to reproduce successfully.

the state treats family members and citizens as two completely unrelated groups of people
choice.ex: 밑줄 해석: 개인들은 국가의 시민으로 여겨지기 전에 우선적으로 가족 구성원으로 이해된다. 해설: 밑줄은 유교 문화에서 개인을 바라보는 '순서' — 가족 구성원이라는 정체성이 국가 시민이라는 정체성보다 앞선다는 뜻이며, ❹ Therefore(가족의 내재적 가치)의 전제가 됨. ②는 before를 시간상의 절차로 읽은 문자적 함정, ③ 시민적 권리 포기는 과장(❻ 기본적 자유·권리는 보장되어야 함), ④ 무관 한 두 집단은 본문에 없음, ⑤ 시민 교육 방식은 본문과 무관. ① 사람들은 시민이 되기를 신청하기 전에 공식적으로 가족과 함께 등록해야 한다 ② 개인은 가족에게 더 잘 봉사하기 위해 시민적 권리를 포기해야 한다 ③ 한 사람의 정체성은 먼저 가족 관계에 의해 규정되고, 그다음에야 국가의 구성원 자격에 의해 규정된다 ④ 아이들은 주로 집에서 부모를 지켜봄으로써 좋은 시민이 되는 법을 배운다 ⑤ 국가는 가족 구성원과 시민을 완전히 무관한 두 집단으로 취급한다
choice.body: In contrast, for Confucian culture, while seeking fair equality of opportunity for individuals is important, the family assumes a fundamental role in human flourishing, and living within a family institution is considered the essential way of life. Individuals are primarily understood as family members before they are regarded as state citizens. Therefore, for Confucians, the family possesses inherent value that should never be abandoned, even if it results in certain societal inequalities.
choice.ul: primarily understood as family members before they are regarded as state citizens.

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
opt: (A) biased — (B) discovered — (C) uncertainty
(A) neutral — (B) shaped — (C) legitimacy
(A) neutral — (B) discovered — (C) legitimacy
(A) biased — (B) shaped — (C) legitimacy
(A) neutral — (B) shaped — (C) uncertainty
choice.ex: (A) neutral (B) shaped (C) legitimacy 근거 ❸❺❻ 해설: (A) ❸ 측정 대상이 ‘단지 관행’이라고 생각하기 어렵다 = 통계는 보통 있는 그대로의 중립적 기록으로 여겨짐, yet 뒤 ‘국가가 만든 범주’와 대조 / (B) ❺ categories ... are devised = 국가가 만들어 냄 / (C) ❻ making decisions without seeming to decide, build trust in authority = 정당성. biased는 yet의 대조가 성립하지 않고 ❸과도 어긋남, discovered는 ❺ devised(고안)와 반대, uncertainty는 ❻ 신뢰 구축과 반대. 요약문 해석: 공식 통계는 흔히 (A) 중립적인 사실의 기록으로 여겨지지만, 그 배후의 범주들은 국가의 정책 목표를 충족하도록 국가에 의해 (B) 만들어진 다. 숫자는 스스로 말해 주는 것처럼 보이기 때문에, 공식적인 선택에 (C) 정당성의 분위기를 부여한다.
choice.psg: ❶ Statistics in the twentieth century became the systematic collection of quantitative information needed by the state. ❷ This process occurred in all the industrialised countries as a key part of their becoming modern states. ❸ Desrosières writes: “It is difficult to think simultaneously that the objects being measured really do exist and that this is only a convention”. ❹ Yet this is the case. ❺ Phenomena such as prices being charged and products being sold exist, but the categories and classification frameworks supporting the collection, aggregation, and organisation of official statistics are devised to serve the purposes of the state, for macroeconomic or for social policies. ❻ Theodore Porter described the use of statistics to create state authority: “Quantification is a way of making decisions without seeming to decide”, characterising it as a “social technology” intended to build trust in authority.
choice.body: Official statistics are often regarded as a (A)________ record of facts, yet the categories behind them are (B)________ by the state to meet its policy goals. Because numbers appear to speak for themselves, they give official choices an air of (C)________.

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

choice.ex: (A) concealing (B) objective (C) confidence 근거 ❻ 해설: (A) ❻ making decisions without seeming to decide = 결정한다는 사실을 숨김 / (B) 숫자가 스스로 결정한 것처럼 보임 = 객관적 / (C) ❻ intended to build trust in authority = 신뢰. highlighting은 ‘결정하는 것처럼 보이지 않음’과 반대, arbitrary(자의적인)로 보이는 수치로는 신뢰를 강화 할 수 없어 문장 논리가 깨짐, suspicion은 trust와 반대. 요약문 해석: Porter는 정량화가 당국으로 하여금 선택이 이루어지고 있다는 사실 자체를 (A) 숨기면서 문제를 결정짓게 해 준다고 주장한다. 수치는 (B) 객관적으로 보이기 때문에, 통계는 통치하는 사람들에 대한 대중의 (C) 신뢰를 강화하는 사회적 도구로 기능한다.
choice.psg: ❶ Statistics in the twentieth century became the systematic collection of quantitative information needed by the state. ❷ This process occurred in all the industrialised countries as a key part of their becoming modern states. ❸ Desrosières writes: “It is difficult to think simultaneously that the objects being measured really do exist and that this is only a convention”. ❹ Yet this is the case. ❺ Phenomena such as prices being charged and products being sold exist, but the categories and classification frameworks supporting the collection, aggregation, and organisation of official statistics are devised to serve the purposes of the state, for macroeconomic or for social policies. ❻ Theodore Porter described the use of statistics to create state authority: “Quantification is a way of making decisions without seeming to decide”, characterising it as a “social technology” intended to build trust in authority.
choice.body: Porter argues that quantification allows authorities to settle matters while (A)________ the fact that a choice is being made at all. Because figures appear (B)________, statistics work as a social tool for strengthening public (C)________ in those who govern.

choice.stem: 위 글의 내용으로부터 추론할 수 없는 것을 고르시오.
opt: Becoming a modern state involved developing systematic ways of gathering numerical data.
The writer suggests that the categories behind official statistics reflect the priorities of the state.
Presenting matters in numbers can help those in power make their choices look less like personal judgments.
Statistical figures can describe things that truly exist even though the way they are grouped is a human agreement.
The writer suggests that official statistics were first developed in response to demands from ordinary citizens.
choice.ex: 원문은 통계를 ‘국가가 필요로 하는(needed by the state)’ 정보로, 범주를 국가 목적에 맞게 고안된 것으로 설명할 뿐 시민의 요구나 통계의 기원은 언급하지 않음(원문 밖 인과). 나머지는 ❸❹❺(실재 + 관행) / ❺(국가 목적에 맞춘 범주) / ❻(결정하는 것처럼 보이지 않음) / ❶❷(근대 국가화의 핵심 요소)에서 추론 가능. ① 근거 ❶❷ — 근대 국가가 되는 것은 수치 자료를 모으는 체계적인 방법을 발전시키는 것을 수반했다. ② 근거 ❺ — 필자는 공식 통계 배후의 범주들이 국가의 우선순위를 반영한다고 시사한다. ③ 근거 ❻ — 문제를 숫자로 제시하는 것은 권력자들이 자신의 선택을 개인적 판단처럼 덜 보이게 하는 데 도움이 될 수 있다. ④ 근거 ❸❹❺ — 통계 수치는 그것들이 분류되는 방식이 인간의 합의일지라도 실제로 존재하는 것들을 묘사할 수 있다. ⑤ 근거 없음(정답) — 필자는 공식 통계가 처음에 일반 시민들의 요구에 응하여 발전되었다고 시사한다.
choice.psg: ❶ Statistics in the twentieth century became the systematic collection of quantitative information needed by the state. ❷ This process occurred in all the industrialised countries as a key part of their becoming modern states. ❸ Desrosières writes: “It is difficult to think simultaneously that the objects being measured really do exist and that this is only a convention”. ❹ Yet this is the case. ❺ Phenomena such as prices being charged and products being sold exist, but the categories and classification frameworks supporting the collection, aggregation, and organisation of official statistics are devised to serve the purposes of the state, for macroeconomic or for social policies. ❻ Theodore Porter described the use of statistics to create state authority: “Quantification is a way of making decisions without seeming to decide”, characterising it as a “social technology” intended to build trust in authority.

choice.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

official figures are deliberately falsified in order to mislead the public

choice.ex: 밑줄 해석: 이것(측정·분류의 방식)은 단지 하나의 관행(사람들이 합의한 약속)일 뿐이다. 해설: convention은 여기서 ‘(사람들이 합의한) 관행·약속’. 대상은 really do exist(실재)하지만 그것을 재고 묶는 틀은 ❺처럼 국가 목적에 맞게 고안된 것. ②는 really do exist와 정면 모순(실재 + 관행이 동시에 성립한다는 것이 핵심), ③은 convention(대회)의 문자적 의미 함정, ④는 difficult를 ‘측정이 어렵다’로 오독, ⑤는 고의 조작이라는 과장. ① 통계는 정부 관리들이 참석하는 정기 대회에서 수집된다 ② 공식 수치는 대중을 오도하기 위해 고의로 조작된다 ③ 측정되는 대상들은 가상의 것이며 실제로 존재하지 않는다 ④ 그 대상들이 분류되고 세어지는 방식은 자연적 사실이 아니라 인간이 만든 약속이다 ⑤ 그러한 대상들을 정확히 측정하는 것은 대부분의 근대 국가의 능력을 넘어선다
choice.body: This process occurred in all the industrialised countries as a key part of their becoming modern states. Desrosières writes: “It is difficult to think simultaneously that the objects being measured really do exist and that this is only a convention”. Yet this is the case.

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

choice.ex: (A) enrich (B) isolated (C) complete 근거 ❶❷❼ 해설: (A) ❶ each perspective ... can potential y enhance the others = 풍부하게 함 / (B) ❷ study in silos, each community sectioned from the others = 고립 / (C) ❼ nobody is an expert in the whole of anything = 전체 그림. undermine은 ❶의 와인 비유(gain much)와 반대, inseparable은 sectioned(구분된)와 반대, narrow는 연구자들이 오히려 좁은 부분만 안다는 내용과 반대. 요약문 해석: 화학을 아는 것이 와인 전문가에게 이롭듯이, 한 분야의 통찰은 다른 분야의 작업을 (A) 풍부하게 할 수 있다. 하지만 각각의 도구와 신체의 각 부분이 너무나 깊은 전문화를 요구하기 때문에, 연구자들은 결국 서로 (B) 고립되고, 오늘날 아무도 (C) 전체 그림을 파악하지 못한다.
choice.psg: ❶ Just as an expert in the taste and colour of wine will gain much by being aware of the chemistry that underlies those qualities, so each perspective on the body can potentially enhance the others. ❷ And yet every scientific tool, from microscopes to mathematics, and every aspect of the body, from the brain to the microorganism, requires such depth of expertise that this tends not to happen: we tend to study the human body in silos, each community sectioned from the others by its own specialised vocabulary. ❸ Research communities may be dedicated to one type of scientific tool or a specific component of the body, such as one type of cell. ❹ How different types of cell communicate with one another becomes its own specialist topic. ❺ Even simple forms of life on Earth are now rarely studied as a whole, and the human body is evidently much more complex. ❻ As long ago as 1890, The Times newspaper commented that knowledge ‘had already become too vast to be manageable’. ❼ Today, nobody is an expert in the whole of anything.

para.en: When a cell divides, the genomes of its two daughters are often not quite identical to each other or to that of the parent cell. On rare occasions, the error may represent a change for the better; more probably, it will cause no significant difference in the cell’s prospects. But in some cases, the error will cause serious damage; for example, by disrupting the coding sequence for a key protein. Changes due to mistakes of the first type will tend to be perpetuated, because the altered cell has an increased likelihood of reproducing itself. Changes due to mistakes of the second type ― neutral changes ― may be perpetuated or not: it is a matter of chance whether the altered cell or its cousins will succeed. But changes that cause serious damage lead nowhere: the cell that suffers them dies, leaving no progeny. Through endless repetition of this cycle of mutation and natural selection organisms evolve: their genetic specifications change, sometimes giving organisms new ways to exploit the environment more effectively, to survive in competition with others, and to reproduce successfully.

Within liberal culture, the value of fair equality of opportunity for individuals outweighs the preservation of the family’s integrity. In contrast, for Confucian culture, while seeking fair equality of opportunity for individuals is important, the family assumes a fundamental role in human flourishing, and living within a family institution is considered the essential way of life. Individuals are primarily understood as family members before they are regarded as state citizens. Therefore, for Confucians, the family possesses inherent value that should never be abandoned, even if it results in certain societal inequalities. Some cultures, like the liberal one, may choose to impose increasing restrictions on the role of families and implement more egalitarian government programs for education, healthcare, and other positive rights in society in the pursuit of fair equality of opportunity. On the other hand, other cultures, like the Confucian one, may prefer to primarily assign welfare responsibilities to the family, accepting inequalities stemming from the existence of the family as long as everyone’s basic freedoms and rights are safeguarded in the state.

Statistics in the twentieth century became the systematic collection of quantitative information needed by the state. This process occurred in all the industrialised countries as a key part of their becoming modern states. Desrosières writes: “It is difficult to think simultaneously that the objects being measured really do exist and that this is only a convention”. Yet this is the case. Phenomena such as prices being charged and products being sold exist, but the categories and classification frameworks supporting the collection, aggregation, and organisation of official statistics are devised to serve the purposes of the state, for macroeconomic or for social policies. Theodore Porter described the use of statistics to create state authority: “Quantification is a way of making decisions without seeming to decide”, characterising it as a “social technology” intended to build trust in authority.

Just as an expert in the taste and colour of wine will gain much by being aware of the chemistry that underlies those qualities, so each perspective on the body can potentially enhance the others. And yet every scientific tool, from microscopes to mathematics, and every aspect of the body, from the brain to the microorganism, requires such depth of expertise that this tends not to happen: we tend to study the human body in silos, each community sectioned from the others by its own specialised vocabulary. Research communities may be dedicated to one type of scientific tool or a specific component of the body, such as one type of cell. How different types of cell communicate with one another becomes its own specialist topic. Even simple forms of life on Earth are now rarely studied as a whole, and the human body is evidently much more complex. As long ago as 1890, The Times newspaper commented that knowledge ‘had already become too vast to be manageable’. Today, nobody is an expert in the whole of anything.

Historically, palaces weren’t just homes; they were carefully constructed stages designed to impress and intimidate. While stone symbolized permanence and strength, glass offered something equally powerful: visibility. The introduction of large windows in palaces allowed rulers to literally look down upon their subjects, emphasizing their elevated position. Conversely, it also allowed subjects to gaze up at their leaders, creating a sense of awe and distance. Consider the Palace of Versailles: its Hall of Mirrors, lined with reflective surfaces, not only magnified the grandeur of the space but also placed the king at the center of a dazzling display, reinforcing his absolute authority. The use of glass in palaces wasn’t merely aesthetic; it was strategic. Open sightlines allowed for better surveillance and control, ensuring the safety and security of the ruling family. Courtiers and visitors were constantly aware of being observed, contributing to an atmosphere of careful obedience and respect. The very architecture dictated social behavior, with glass acting as a silent enforcer of the power dynamic.
